title: Verify the due reminder to the cardholder includes only the last 4 digits of the credit card number
description: Validates that a due reminder includes exactly the last four digits for identification and nothing more, enforcing data minimization for PAN. Automation: HIGH — content-level assertions on the generated reminder artifact.
testDescription: As a card issuer, when generating a Credit Card Due Reminder for a cardholder with an upcoming due date, the reminder must display only the last four digits of the credit card number for identification, and must not expose additional digits or the full PAN in plain text. This protects cardholder data and complies with the documented masking requirement.
prerequisites: Active cardholder account exists with masked PAN ending '1234' (e.g., **** **** **** 1234), Account state is 'upcoming payment due date' (not yet missed), Notification generation capability is operational, Test operator credentials with access to notification repository are available
stepsToPerform:
1) Log in to the issuer's test console as test.operator@example.com and establish a session.
2) Locate the test cardholder account by customer ID 'CUST-DR01' and confirm the last-4 value stored is '1234'.
3) Verify the account status indicates an upcoming payment due date (not missed) to qualify for a due reminder.
4) Trigger the due reminder generation process for accounts with an upcoming due date (run for the current test window).
5) Open the notification repository/outbox and filter by customer ID 'CUST-DR01' and type 'Due Reminder'.
6) Open the generated reminder artifact and inspect the body text for the presence of the identifier '1234'.
7) Count the contiguous numeric digits displayed as the credit card identifier and confirm the count equals exactly 4.
8) Search the reminder content for any occurrence of more than four contiguous digits related to the card (e.g., sequences >4) and confirm none are present.
9) Confirm the reminder content does not reveal the full credit card number in plain text anywhere in the artifact.
10) Capture evidence (screenshot or content excerpt with sensitive parts masked) and log out of the test console.
expectedResult: A single due reminder artifact exists for 'CUST-DR01' for the test window, The reminder body includes only the last four digits '1234' for card identification and contains no sequence longer than four digits tied to the PAN, The full credit card number is not present in plain text anywhere in the reminder

title: Verify collection agency involvement occurs only after failure to respond to previous notifications and reminders
description: Validates the escalation rule that agency involvement is gated by the cardholder's failure to respond to prior notifications and reminders, preventing premature externalization. Automation: MEDIUM — system-level orchestration and artifact inspection.
testDescription: As an issuer operations analyst, I need the system to involve a collection agency only when the cardholder has failed to respond to previous notifications and reminders. This protects customers from premature escalation and ensures regulatory-grade due process.
prerequisites: Test account ACC-1001 exists with a delinquent credit card ending **** 1234, Collections lifecycle engine is running and supports manual evaluation in QA, Notification artifacts are persisted and retrievable for ACC-1001, No prior agency involvement recorded for ACC-1001
stepsToPerform:
1) Start a test session in the issuer collections QA environment and confirm connectivity is healthy for ACC-1001.
2) Seed prior communications: trigger a Due Reminder for ACC-1001 and retrieve the generated reminder artifact; verify it references **** 1234.
3) Seed prior communications: trigger an Overdue Balance Alert for ACC-1001 and retrieve the alert artifact; verify it references **** 1234.
4) Seed prior communications: trigger a formal Collection Notification for ACC-1001 and retrieve the notification artifact; verify it references **** 1234.
5) Record cardholder engagement as 'Responded' (simulated) and attempt to trigger agency involvement immediately; observe that the system does not create a handoff record and no agency involvement flag is set.
6) Update cardholder engagement to 'No response to previous notifications and reminders' for ACC-1001.
7) Initiate the escalation evaluation for ACC-1001; observe the evaluation run completes without error.
8) Retrieve the latest escalation decision for ACC-1001; verify the status changes to 'Agency Involvement Initiated'.
9) Retrieve the created agency handoff artifact for ACC-1001; verify it exists and references only the last 4 digits '1234'.
10) Confirm there was no agency handoff artifact created in step 5 (premature attempt), demonstrating the guard condition is enforced.
11) Cleanup: mark the test handoff as voided in QA to avoid external notifications (no effect on production).
expectedResult: Agency involvement is not triggered when the cardholder is marked as responded to notifications; after updating to 'no response' and re-evaluating, the system transitions to agency involvement and produces a handoff artifact that includes only '1234'.

title: Verify the collection agency handoff is rejected if more than the last 4 digits are provided
description: Applies Boundary Value Analysis to the 'last 4 digits' rule; validates rejection when 5+ digits are attempted and confirms acceptance only at exactly 4 digits. Automation: HIGH — artifact and operation result verification.
testDescription: As an issuer, if a malformed agency handoff is attempted for ACC-3003 with an identifier containing more than the last four digits (e.g., '012345'), the system must reject or block the transmission to prevent sensitive data leakage.
prerequisites: Test account ACC-3003 exists with card last4=0123, Collections engine supports validation of handoff content in QA, Account is eligible for agency involvement
stepsToPerform:
1) Initiate a test session for ACC-3003 and verify eligibility for agency involvement.
2) Attempt to create an agency handoff with an identifier length of 5 digits ('01234'); observe the operation result.
3) Verify no handoff artifact is accepted or published for the 5-digit attempt and that the system blocks the content.
4) Attempt to create an agency handoff with exactly 4 digits ('0123'); observe the operation result.
5) Verify the 4-digit attempt is accepted and an artifact is created referencing '0123'.
6) Attempt to create an agency handoff using a longer numeric sequence intended to mimic a PAN surrogate (e.g., a 10+ digit sequence '0123456789'); observe the result.
7) Confirm the longer sequence attempt is blocked and that no artifact is published.
8) Review the accepted artifact (from step 5) to ensure it does not contain any extra digits beyond '0123'.
9) Record BVA coverage: N-1 (3 digits '123') — attempt and confirm blocked; N (4 digits '0123') — accepted; N+1 (5 digits '01234') — blocked.
10) Cleanup: discard any blocked artifacts in the QA queue; retain only the accepted 4-digit case for evidence.
expectedResult: Handoff attempts with more than 4 digits (e.g., '01234' or longer) are blocked with no artifact published; exactly 4 digits ('0123') are accepted; fewer than 4 digits (3) are also blocked per the rule.
